edges.rationale: MSkill suggested learning order: study AI fundamentals before Generative AI. This is editorial sequencing, not a universal technical requirement or a Microsoft prerequisite.
MSkill suggested learning order: study Generative AI before Prompt design. This is editorial sequencing, not a universal technical requirement or a Microsoft prerequisite.
MSkill suggested learning order: study Generative AI before AI agents. This is editorial sequencing, not a universal technical requirement or a Microsoft prerequisite.
MSkill editorial connection: data modeling helps organize structured knowledge. It is not a universal prerequisite for adding a document as an agent knowledge source.
MSkill suggested learning order: study Knowledge sources before Retrieval and grounding. This is editorial sequencing, not a universal technical requirement or a Microsoft prerequisite.
MSkill suggested learning order: study API fundamentals before Agent actions and tools. This is editorial sequencing, not a universal technical requirement or a Microsoft prerequisite.
MSkill suggested learning order: study Business process mapping before Cloud flows. This is editorial sequencing, not a universal technical requirement or a Microsoft prerequisite.
MSkill suggested learning order: study Business process mapping before App user experience. This is editorial sequencing, not a universal technical requirement or a Microsoft prerequisite.
MSkill editorial connection: Microsoft Entra ID is an identity platform relevant to access control. The general access-control concept does not require this specific product.
MSkill suggested learning order: study Governance before Monitoring and evaluation. This is editorial sequencing, not a universal technical requirement or a Microsoft prerequisite.
MSkill suggested learning order: study Application lifecycle management before Solution deployment. This is editorial sequencing, not a universal technical requirement or a Microsoft prerequisite.
MSkill suggested learning order: study Prompt design before AI agents. This is editorial sequencing, not a universal technical requirement or a Microsoft prerequisite.
Cloud flows are a Power Automate workflow category; this hierarchy does not make every automation a cloud flow.
MSkill editorial connection: app user experience is a design concern when building Power Apps; the general skill is not a component owned by Power Apps.
Configured tools can extend an agent with service operations. Tools are optional; an agent does not inherently have every available action.
MSkill editorial connection: an agent may consult knowledge sources. Those sources can exist independently of the agent and are not necessarily part of it.
MSkill connects Microsoft 365 Copilot with generative AI to explain generated assistance in work contexts; availability depends on the licensed experience.
Copilot Studio provides an environment for authoring agents. Publishing and available features depend on the selected experience and tenant requirements.
Power Automate supports building cloud flows around triggers and actions; the specific services used determine connection requirements.
Canvas apps provide controls and layouts for application interfaces. MSkill treats interface design as a broader skill than using this product.
Dataverse supports tables and relationships for business data models. Choosing an appropriate model remains a design task.
Connectors expose service operations for automation. Individual operations still require their configured connections and permissions.
Knowledge sources supply material for retrieval-based grounding; their presence alone does not guarantee relevant or correct answers.
Entra ID supports identity and access management. MSkill distinguishes that implementation from the broader access-control discipline.
MSkill recommends describing a process trigger, desired result and exceptions before automating it. This is planning advice, not a product prerequisite.
Understanding API inputs, outputs and errors helps when designing custom tools. Using a prebuilt tool need not require writing an API.
Generative AI can support agents that interpret requests and produce responses. This relationship does not imply every agent uses a generative model.
Copilot Studio and Power Automate have connected flow authoring scenarios. Check the documented flow type, environment and billing requirements before reuse.
Copilot Studio supports SharePoint knowledge sources. Access depends on the source configuration and authentication; connecting a site is not blanket permission.
Copilot Studio can use Dataverse tables as knowledge with the documented search, authentication and permission setup.
A canvas app control can trigger a Power Automate flow. App and flow connections must be configured for the intended users.
Power Apps can build on Dataverse tables. This is a supported data option, not a requirement for every canvas app.
A Power Automate flow can use a Teams connector action, such as posting a message, through an authorized connection.
The SharePoint connector provides list and library triggers and actions for Power Automate flows.
The Dataverse connector exposes data operations and triggers to Power Automate; the chosen connection must have the required access.
Custom server-side logic, including Azure Functions, can be exposed to Power Automate through an API connector. This requires deliberate API and authentication configuration.
Microsoft Graph exposes supported Teams APIs. An application must request the permissions required by each operation.
Microsoft Graph exposes supported SharePoint APIs. The available operation and granted permissions determine which content an application can access.
MSkill links the Microsoft 365 assistance experience with Copilot Studio agent authoring. These are distinct products; licensing and deployment choices must be checked separately.
Copilot Studio agents can be configured with knowledge sources. Source selection is optional and should match the intended questions.
Copilot Studio agents can call configured tools. Tool availability and authorization must be established before an agent can use them.
Copilot Studio can use Power Platform connectors to expose service operations as tools; a connector is not an automatic grant of access.
Cloud flows can use connector triggers and actions. A flow does not automatically use every connector or service.
Dataverse is used by model-driven apps and can supply data to canvas apps. Canvas apps can also use other data sources.
Knowledge-grounded agents can retrieve source material to inform responses. Retrieval is one design pattern, not a requirement for every agent.
HTTP-triggered Azure Functions receive requests and return responses. API design knowledge is relevant to that pattern; other trigger types exist.
Power Platform data policies can restrict Copilot Studio capabilities and connections. Effective controls depend on the applicable tenant and environment policies.
MSkill recommends reviewing Power Automate environment access and data policies before sharing automations.
MSkill recommends reviewing Power Apps sharing, environment access and data policies before making an app available to others.
MSkill treats authentication and allowed tool access as agent design decisions. Instructions alone are not an authorization boundary.
Access behavior differs between knowledge-source types. Review each source configuration; do not assume uploaded content inherits per-user source permissions.
Dataverse provides security controls for data access. Review the effective roles and permissions for the intended users.
Power Platform administration provides controls for environments, users and policies; governance also requires organizational decisions and ownership.
Solution deployment involves target environments and administrative permissions. MSkill links this practice to Power Platform administration.
MSkill connects lifecycle management with environment administration when planning release ownership and operational support.
Power Platform solutions package components for movement between environments as part of a managed lifecycle.
MSkill recommends testing agent conversations and inspecting behavior before release. Design-time testing does not prove production-channel behavior.
MSkill suggested learning order: study API fundamentals before Microsoft Graph. This is editorial sequencing, not a universal technical requirement or a Microsoft prerequisite.
HTTP-triggered functions are a practical setting for learning request and response contracts; this is an editorial learning connection.
MSkill connects prebuilt Foundry Tools with agent solution design as an optional capability choice, not a required agent platform.
Foundry Tools and generative-model APIs are distinct capability families. MSkill links them for comparison when choosing an AI solution approach.
MSkill uses Dataverse tables and relationships as one concrete setting for practicing data modeling.
SharePoint is a supported source option for Copilot Studio knowledge. Relevance and access must be reviewed for the selected site content.
Teams offers Copilot experiences in collaboration workflows; exact availability depends on licensing and administrator configuration.
MSkill recommends reviewed deployment, ownership and rollback decisions as part of release governance.
Application lifecycle management includes governance across development, deployment and maintenance; it is broader than packaging a release.
Copilot Studio provides conversation testing and activity inspection. MSkill recommends recording expected and observed outcomes separately.
MSkill links Power Apps to interface design practice: clear controls, readable layouts and useful feedback still require deliberate design.
A business process supplies context for choosing what a flow should automate. The relationship is editorial planning guidance.
MSkill treats access decisions as one part of governance, alongside ownership and operational policy.
Agent flows can perform multi-step operations for an agent. Check the supported flow pattern before treating an existing cloud flow as an agent tool.
